name: The Pacific War: From Pearl Harbor to the Bomb
description: Carrier battles, island campaigns and the first atomic weapons: how the war in the Pacific began in December 1941 and ended in 1945.

checkpoints.name: The road to war
checkpoints.note: The Empire of Japan grew strong after 1868 and took Manchuria, where it set up Manchukuo in 1932. Hirohito was emperor, and in 1939 World War II began in Europe.

checkpoints.name: Pearl Harbor to Midway
checkpoints.note: Japan struck the American fleet at Pearl Harbor, and Franklin D. Roosevelt brought the United States into the war. Admiral Yamamoto planned the attack, the Japanese took Singapore, and Nimitz won the Battle of Midway.

checkpoints.name: Island by island
checkpoints.note: Allied forces under Nimitz and MacArthur advanced across the Pacific. The new Boeing B-29 bombers were built to reach Japan, and the Manhattan Project worked in secret on a new weapon.

checkpoints.name: The bomb and surrender
checkpoints.note: The Trinity test showed that the bomb worked, and Harry S. Truman met his allies at the Potsdam conference. Atomic bombs fell on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, Japan surrendered. The giant battleship Yamato was sunk in April 1945, and Japan, under a new constitution, was rebuilt after the Tokyo trials.
